audit_reason: Retrospective analysis attributed to Oelke, 786 treatment-naive men >=40 with LUTS, median BCI 73->188 and Wmax 9.6->23 W/m2 across Schaefer grades 0-6, and grade-adjustment of BCI<100 / Wmax<7 thresholds all match. The crucial cross-sectional-not-within-man distinction is preserved. 'The review suggests' lightly compresses the study-as-reported-by-review attribution but stays inside the already-established review frame.

locator: PREOPERATIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF PATIENTS WITH VOIDING DYSFUNCTION, development and verification paragraphs; FIGURE 2 caption; FIGURE 3 caption; Recent findings; REFERENCES AND RECOMMENDED READING, reference 23 annotation
text: Rademakers et al. (rademakers2016.pdf.md), a narrative review, report that Oelke developed the Hannover–Maastricht nomogram from urodynamic data of 822 treatment-naïve men aged ≥40 with LUTS/BPO. It plots bladder-outlet-obstruction index against maximum Watts factor to classify outlet resistance and detrusor contractility simultaneously; values below the 25th-percentile line indicate detrusor underactivity relative to outlet resistance, including when obstruction coexists. Validation remained ongoing.
audit_reason: Faithful: Oelke-developed nomogram, 822 treatment-naive men >=40 with LUTS/BPO, BOOI-vs-maximum-Watts-factor axes classifying outlet resistance and detrusor contractility simultaneously, sub-25th-percentile = detrusor underactivity relative to outlet resistance including with coexisting obstruction, and ongoing validation are all preserved with review attribution. Dropping 'and colleagues' is immaterial.

locator: Main-text PATIENTS AND METHODS; RESULTS, TABLE 1; DISCUSSION, paragraph beginning “Based on these results”
text: He et al. (he2010.pdf.md, PATIENTS AND METHODS; RESULTS, TABLE 1) report a retrospective, uncontrolled series of 21 men with nonbacterial chronic prostatitis and dysfunctional voiding whose Qmax rose 8.2 (SD 4.1) to 15.1 (SD 7.3) mL/s after ~10 weeks of relaxation/coordination biofeedback, not strengthening (P<0.05); antibiotics, α-blockers, anticholinergics suspended. audit_reason: All quantities (21 men, Qmax 8.2(4.1)->15.1(7.3) mL/s, ~10 wk, P<0.05), the uncontrolled retrospective design, the relaxation-coordination-not-strengthening distinction, and the no-controlled-effect caveat match the FRD. Dropping 'throughout the sessions' from the med-suspension note and omitting session length/frequency (~30 min, 2-3x/wk) are compressions that do not distort the validated claim.

The 'not validated or baseline-equivalent' guard is preserved; the baseline p-value lets the reader see the difference is non-significant, not proven equivalent. Dropping baseline SDs is minor compression.

(masterson2017.pdf.md, Methods; Results) prospectively studied an uncontrolled pilot of multimodal pelvic-floor physical therapy (manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, biofeedback, neuromodulation; nonstandardized frequency) in 14 men with idiopathic CPPS, assessed at the tenth visit. audit_reason: Uncontrolled pilot, 14 men with idiopathic CPPS, multimodal components, nonstandardized frequency, tenth-visit assessment, and the 10-completed / 4-ongoing split with the ongoing-not-dropout/failure qualifier all match the FRD. Pain-vs-urinary outcomes and the Anderson 2011 strand are outside this FRD, so their absence is not a defect.

text: Anderson et al. (anderson2011.pdf.md), a prospective open-label UCPPS pilot, report 113 of 157 (72%; 106 men, 7 women) completed six months of internal therapeutic-wand use within a multimodal self-treatment program (prescribed 3–4×/week; withdrawal threshold <1×/week). audit_reason: Design (prospective open-label UCPPS pilot), completion (113/157, 72%; 106 men/7 women), multimodal self-treatment context, prescribed 3-4x/week with <1x/week withdrawal threshold, and withdrawal-reason counts (10 noncompliance, 10 questionnaire, rest unspecified) are FRD-supported, and the witness correctly refuses a perceived-inefficacy partition and the male-only clinic-PFPT framing. Omitted 109-outcome-data and withdrawal-timing split are non-material refinements.

locator: Abstract, Materials and Methods; §2.3 Study design; §3 Results; §3.3 Voided volume; Tables 2–4, voided-volume rows
text: In Shirazi et al.'s single-center, randomized, double-blind 12-week BPH trial (60 men, 30/group), pentoxifylline 400 mg every eight hours plus tamsulosin 0.4 mg/day versus placebo plus tamsulosin showed no significant between-group voided-volume change (0.80 versus +1.34 mL; p=.22) and no statistically significant within-group change (p=.90, .89). Baseline-to-endpoint voided-volume only—not residual or flow; visit schedule, onset, post-withdrawal persistence unestablished (Comparison-between-combination-of-tamsulosin-and-Pentoxifylline-versus-tamsulosin-alone-in.pdf.md, §3.3).
audit_reason: All figures and scope match the FRD: Shirazi et al. single-center, randomized, double-blind 12-week trial, 60 men (30/group), PTX 400 mg q8h + tamsulosin 0.4 mg/day vs placebo + tamsulosin; between-group voided-volume change 0.80 vs +1.34 mL, p=.22; within-group p=.90 and .89; results limited to voided volume, not PVR or Qmax. Crucially it answers the producing question without violating its constraint: it conveys the baseline-to-endpoint (12-week) measurement frame yet explicitly marks intermediate visit schedule, onset, and post-withdrawal persistence as unestablished rather than inferring onset from the final result. Dropped dispersion (±35.81/±50.79) and percent-change columns are non-material; the FRD itself flagged the ± values as of unidentified type.

text: Roberts et al. report that pentoxifylline 5 μmol/L added to healthy volunteers' whole blood (30-minute preincubation, 37°C) reduced FMLP-stimulated neutrophil intracellular oxidant (DCF hydrogen-peroxide) production to 76 ± 5% of the PTX-free response (mean ± SE; n=10; p<0.025). text: Delanian et al. 2003, single-center randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 2×2 factorial trial in women with superficial radiation-induced fibrosis >6 months after breast radiotherapy (24 eligible, 22 with 6-month data). Combination pentoxifylline 800 mg/day plus vitamin E 1000 U/day gave −60.2% versus double-placebo −42.6% surface-area change (P=.038, Wilcoxon). Two-way ANOVA found no significant main effects, only a PTX×vitamin-E interaction trend (P=.09).
audit_reason: Design (single-center RDBPC 2x2 factorial, women, superficial RIF >6 months post-breast-RT, 24 eligible/22 with 6-month data), the combination doses, the -60.2% vs -42.6% surface-area change with P=.038 Wilcoxon, and crucially the ANOVA no-significant-main-effects / interaction-trend P=.09 (answering the PTX-monotherapy-failure ask) are all preserved. The omitted per-group n and area-vs-patient caveat weaken completeness, but the explicit ANOVA null prevents over-reading, so the witness is not materially misleading.

locator: Modalities of Combined PTX-vitE Treatment; Statistical Analysis; Primary Analyses, paragraph beginning “After stopping PTX-vitE: Rebound effect”; DISCUSSION, paragraph beginning “Long-term follow-up of our patients”
text: Delanian et al.'s follow-up of women with superficial breast radiation-induced fibrosis on pentoxifylline 800 mg/day plus vitamin E 1,000 U/day found that, after stopping, fibrosis surface area rebounded more after short (6-12-month) treatment than long (24-48-month) treatment: 40%/year (95% CI 24-56) versus 8.5%/year (95% CI 1-16); P=.0012. Duration was not randomized; follow-up lasted two years (delanian2005.pdf.md).
audit_reason: Women with superficial breast radiation-induced fibrosis, PTX 800 mg/day + vitamin E 1,000 U/day, post-discontinuation rebound greater after short than long treatment (40%/yr [24-56] vs 8.5%/yr [1-16]; P=.0012), non-randomized duration allocation, and the two-year follow-up all match the FRD. The omitted cohort denominators (7 women/8 sites; 37 women/47 sites) and three-patient crossover reduce detail but not the headline position; the wide CIs already signal the small short-treatment basis, so the omission is non-material.

audit_reason: Retrospective chart review of male patients, one ambulatory clinic, April-September 2022, 52 of 120 referred scheduled and attended >=1 PFPT visit (43.3%), and the initial-attendance-not-completion/abandonment/response bound all match the validated claim. Correctly avoids inventing the excluded scheduling-denominator figure.

text: Kassar et al.'s systematic review/meta-analysis of four depression RCTs (318 participants) found no significant difference in all-cause discontinuation between pentoxifylline and placebo: 14/159 versus 16/159; pooled RR 0.88 (95% CI 0.45-1.74; P=0.72). Dosing was 400 mg twice daily (one trial thrice), mostly added to an SSRI; no follow-up limited long-term safety; alpha-blocker-specific safety was not assessed (s00210-025-03845-1.pdf.md).
audit_reason: Four RCTs / 318 participants, 14/159 vs 16/159, RR 0.88 (0.45-1.74, P=0.72), dosing 400 mg BID (one trial TID), mostly SSRI adjunct, the review-acknowledged no-follow-up long-term-safety limit, and the alpha-blocker source gap all match the FRD. The [INFERRED] 'not equivalent safety' caveat is dropped, but the endpoint-specific framing plus the visible CI prevent over-reading; the monotherapy/CAD trial detail is omitted (minor). Non-material.

text: In Parker et al.'s randomized, investigator-blinded porcine haemorrhage-plus-E.-coli-peritonitis experiment (female Large White pigs; n=5 per group), pentoxifylline plus colloid (20 mg/kg bolus, then 20 mg/kg over 60 minutes) gave lower median 2-hour MAP than colloid-plus-saline placebo: 62(10) versus 92(10) mmHg (P<0.01); by 6 hours groups did not differ. audit_reason: Randomized investigator-blinded porcine haemorrhage+E. coli peritonitis, n=5/group, PTX 20 mg/kg bolus then 20 mg/kg over 60 min, 2-hour MAP 62(10) vs 92(10) mmHg (P<0.01), 6-hour no difference, and the acute-not-chronic-oral scope all match. Polarity (PTX lower MAP) is correctly conveyed. Minor: '(10)' is not labeled as IQR and the 3-hour significant point is dropped, neither material.

locator: Abstract: Design, Interventions, Results; MATERIALS AND METHODS → THE PORCINE MODEL and EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; RESULTS opening paragraph; COMMENT, “In our studies, the administration of pentoxifylline 2 hours” and “If pentoxifylline is administered to animals in uncorrected septic shock”
text: In Ridings et al.'s nonrandomized controlled porcine sepsis experiment (ridings1994.pdf.md, COMMENT), intravenous pentoxifylline (20 mg/kg bolus, 6 mg/kg/h) begun two hours after Pseudomonas infusion (established, uncorrected shock) was followed by fatal hypotension within one hour in 2/4 animals; two survivors resembled 1-hour-treated protection (data not shown). Authors attributed deaths to pentoxifylline but said n=4 precluded statistics; untransferable to bladder dysfunction.
audit_reason: Nonrandomized porcine model, dose/route (20 mg/kg bolus + 6 mg/kg/h), 2-hour delayed start in established uncorrected shock, 2/4 fatal hypotension within one hour, survivor resemblance to 1-hour-treated protection (data not shown), the authors' attribution, and the small-sample caveat all match. The untransferable-to-bladder scope is appropriate.

locator: MATERIALS AND METHODS; paragraphs beginning “A retrospective analysis,” “Patient symptoms were evaluated,” and “Biofeedback training”
text: In Kaplan et al.'s retrospective study of 43 men with pseudodyssynergia previously misdiagnosed as chronic nonbacterial prostatitis, success of biofeedback was defined as a decrease in symptoms of at least 50% on two consecutive office visits, using the American Urological Association symptom score. This definition measures symptom response, not attendance, completion, or abandonment (kaplan1997.pdf.md, Materials and Methods).
audit_reason: Exactly reproduces the validated definition (>=50% symptom decrease on two consecutive office visits), the AUA instrument, and the 43-man pseudodyssynergia cohort, and correctly bounds it to symptom response rather than attendance/completion. 'Abandonment' is a legitimate extension responsive to the producing question and true of a symptom-reduction definition. Numerator/83% content belongs to a sibling FRD, not this one.

locator: ABSTRACT (Methods); METHODS; RESULTS; Table 1, “Renal Function Parameters at 48 Hours After Ischemia/Reperfusion of the Solitary Left Kidney”; DISCUSSION
text: Wystrychowski et al. (wystrychowski2014.pdf.md, Table 1; RESULTS) randomized 58 male Sprague-Dawley rats; after right nephrectomy, solitary left pedicle was clamped 45 minutes. Subcutaneous pentoxifylline 100 mg/kg versus saline improved 48-hour creatinine clearance only when given 60 minutes before ischemia (10/arm; P<.001), not 1 minute into ischemia or 60 minutes post-release. These within-timing acute-model results don't transfer to chronic bladder disease.
audit_reason: Species, surgery, 45-min clamp, SC PTX 100 mg/kg vs saline, the single protective timing (60 min before ischemia; 10/arm; P<.001) versus the two null timings, and the acute-model/no-transfer scope are preserved. Omitted details (10-week age, 2-week post-nephrectomy interval, null-arm n, explicit no-interaction caveat) are secondary and introduce no error; 'within-timing' preserves the key inferential guard.

locator: Author byline; opening abstract; PREVALENCE AND EPIDEMIOLOGY OF DETRUSOR UNDERACTIVITY, concluding two paragraphs and paragraph beginning “Unlike other researchers, Groutz et al.”
text: Yu and Jeong's clinical literature review (2020ICU_icu-58-S68.pdf.md, PREVALENCE AND EPIDEMIOLOGY OF DETRUSOR UNDERACTIVITY) reports most published detrusor-underactivity prevalence data came from community-dwelling cohorts with significant LUTS judged by arbitrary urodynamic criteria (25%–48% elderly men, 12%–24% women), with limited general-population applicability. Community-based research is described as rare, not absent; one study used free Qmax and post-void residual, not pressure-flow parameters.
audit_reason: These all match the repaired FRD: attribution to Yu and Jeong's clinical literature review, the LUTS-cohort and arbitrary-urodynamic-criteria basis, limited general-population applicability, community research described as 'rare, not absent', and the one study that used free Qmax/PVR rather than pressure-flow parameters. Both repairs are preserved: no universal invasive-PFS sampling and no claimed absence of community surveys. The added prevalence ranges are taken verbatim from the FRD source text, with the applicability caveat attached. '12%-24% women' drops the source's 'elderly' qualifier. That is a minor age-scope slip on an estimate the male-focused question does not ask about, so it is not material.

locator: §2.1 Patient selection; §3 Results, Table 1 and accompanying etiologic-analysis paragraph; §4 Discussion, final limitations paragraph
text: Li et al. 2018 (li2018.pdf.md, §2.1 Patient selection; §3 Results), single-center retrospective at the China Rehabilitation Research Centre, selected an underactive-bladder cohort from 4,538 consecutive LUTS patients undergoing video-urodynamics (December 2004–January 2016); 1,460/1,726 (84.6%) classified neurogenic UAB—a rehabilitation-hospital etiologic distribution, not community prevalence. This FRD carries no sex/age composition, diagnostic criteria, prior-treatment-failure, or shy-bladder data.
audit_reason: Every asserted fact matches the FRD: single-center retrospective at the China Rehabilitation Research Centre, UAB cohort drawn from 4,538 consecutive LUTS patients on video-urodynamics (Dec 2004-Jan 2016), 1,460/1,726 (84.6%) neurogenic. The question's primary scope guard ('selected clinic series must not become a national cohort estimate') is delivered verbatim in substance via 'rehabilitation-hospital etiologic distribution, not community prevalence'. The witness honestly flags absent dimensions (sex/age, diagnostic criteria, prior-treatment-failure, shy bladder). Two minor, non-material imperfections: the locator is abbreviated (drops the Table-1/etiologic paragraph and the Discussion limitations paragraph that the FRD verdict said to add), and the gap list is non-exhaustive (omits pressure-flow/baseline-symptom/obstruction). Neither changes the reader's recovered position, so no repair is compelled.

locator: RESULTS, paragraph beginning “Ten patients completed all six biofeedback sessions”; MATERIAL AND METHODS, paragraph beginning “The biofeedback program is a standardized protocol”
text: Clemens et al. 2000: cohort of 19 men with chronic pelvic pain syndrome receiving combined biofeedback-directed pelvic-floor re-education and bladder training over six biweekly sessions. Ten completed all six, five completed three to five, four completed fewer than three; the four non-completers' reasons were sufficient improvement (2), insurance issues (1), unknown (1). Complete follow-up covered 16 patients, not all enrolled.
audit_reason: 19 men with CPPS, combined biofeedback-directed pelvic-floor re-education plus bladder training over six biweekly sessions, the 10/5/4 completion split, the four non-completers' reasons (sufficient improvement 2, insurance issues 1, unknown 1), and the 16-patient follow-up (from the FRD source text) all match, with the repaired wording preserved. Program components and urinary-vs-flow/residual outcomes are outside the FRD claim.

locator: §2 Methods; §3 Results, opening paragraph and Table 1, Results pre- and post-treatment; §4 Discussion, paragraph beginning Although we realize
text: In Cornel et al.'s uncontrolled pre/post study of men with type III CP/CPPS, 31 of 33 enrolled remained after two dropped out. The mean NIH-CPSI micturition score fell from 5.1 (range 0-10) before to 2.2 (range 0-6) after pelvic-floor biofeedback and re-education (p<0.001). These are symptom scores, not measured urinary flow or residual volume (cornel2005.pdf.md, Results).
audit_reason: Uncontrolled pre/post design, 31 of 33 analyzed after two dropouts, NIH-CPSI micturition 5.1(0-10)->2.2(0-6), p<0.001, and the symptom-not-objective caveat match the FRD claim. The source's dropout reasons (one untrainable, one stopped after three sessions) are not elevated into the validated claim and do not establish abandonment-due-to-ineffectiveness, so their omission is not material.

The five-occasion null is paraphrased as 'no reduction' versus the source's 'did not lower to subnormal values' - a minor precision loss, not a polarity change, that leaves the target-engagement-not-clinical-benefit point intact.
